definition: Document AI, also known as Document Intelligence, refers to a field of technology that employs machine learning (ML) techniques, such as natural language processing (NLP).
details: These techniques are used to develop computer models capable of analyzing documents in a manner akin to human review. Through NLP, computer systems are able to understand relationships and contextual nuances in document contents, which facilitates the extraction of information and insights. Additionally, this technology enables the categorization and organization of the documents themselves. The applications of Document AI extend to processing and parsing a variety of semi-structured documents, such as forms, tables, receipts, invoices, tax forms, contracts, loan agreements, and financial reports.

explainer.lead: Document AI uses machine learning, including natural language processing, to read and organize documents in ways that resemble human review. It matters because useful information is often locked inside forms, invoices, contracts, and reports rather than stored in tidy databases.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a helper sorting a huge pile of school forms, receipts, and letters. The helper can find important details, put similar papers into groups, and tell you what they contain. Document AI teaches computers to do that kind of reading and sorting.
tiers.practitioner: Document AI is applied to semi-structured inputs such as forms, tables, receipts, invoices, contracts, and financial reports. Models use NLP to capture context and relationships, then support field extraction, document categorization, and organization. Outputs should be treated as model predictions, particularly where wording or document structure varies.
tiers.paperLevel: Document AI is the application of machine-learning models, including NLP models, to document analysis, information extraction, and document categorization. NLP provides a way to model relationships and contextual nuances in document contents. Its scope includes semi-structured documents, whose information is not presented as a single uniform record format.

explainer.example: Given an invoice, a Document AI system can extract the supplier name, total, and due date, classify the file as an invoice, and place it with other invoices for later processing.

explainer.intuition: Instead of treating a document as an opaque file, Document AI interprets its contents so a computer can find useful details and decide how the document should be grouped.
howItWorks: Take in semi-structured documents such as forms, tables, or invoices.
Apply machine-learning and NLP techniques to analyze their contents.
Use context and relationships within the text to identify information and insights.
Extract the relevant information from each document.
Categorize and organize the documents themselves.
explainer.whyItMatters: It turns documents that would otherwise require manual reading into information that can be extracted, searched, grouped, and used in further processing.
misconceptions: It is not just document storage: it analyzes content as well as organizing files.
It is not limited to neatly structured records: semi-structured documents are a central use case.
Human-like review does not mean human understanding: the analysis is performed by learned computer models.
